top_story.headline: Immigration agency locks in Amentum for a $2.8 billion Camp East Montana detention contract without competition
top_story.dek: A justification posted today definitizes the letter contract with a total estimated value of $2,796,540,325 across a base period and three options.
paragraphs: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to definitize a letter contract with Amentum Services Inc. for detention and facility management services at Camp East Montana, with no competition. The justification (J&A-26-0098, Rev. 1) puts the total estimated value at $2,796,540,325.26: a seven-month base period at $477,534,464, a 12-month first option at $1,114,884,768, six-month second and third options at $566,972,132 and $580,019,771, and a further $57,129,190.19 line. The document says the value "has increased from the original letter contract planning value due to the increased duration of performance and the continued operational requirement."

The agency's stated reason is that Amentum owns and controls the facility infrastructure, so no other vendor could provide uninterrupted services without disruption and transition costs. The justification says the contract was originally issued by the Department of the Army on July 18, 2025, and that the agency "was not the source selection authority," so the contract and its Performance Work Statement "did not accurately reflect" its operational needs. It says the agency decided that terminating the prior arrangement was in the government's best interest while "the use of the facility was still a priority." It also says a preliminary report from the agency's Office of Detention Oversight is among the circumstances that created "the need for immediate contractual action."

The document says alternatives such as moving to another provider, splitting the requirement or relocating detainees "were considered and determined impracticable," citing the facility's occupancy and "the lack of available bedspace nationwide." It describes the extra duration and cost as necessary "while ICE maintains continuity of operations and evaluates longer-term alternatives." An earlier version of the justification was posted July 22; this revision was posted today.

sections.headline: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency gives Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory up to $499.8 million without competition
paragraphs: There were 48 new justifications, 18 of them posted under other notice types, and none were left out as repeats from earlier editions. The Camp East Montana contract is today's Top Story and 13 contract extensions are in the Extensions section, which leaves 34 here. Four stand out as cards, and the rest are listed below.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency gives Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory a five-year, $499.8 million contract ceiling without competition
meta: Johns Hopkins University, Applied Physics Laboratory
required by law (to maintain an essential research and development capability)
blocks.text: The justification covers an indefinite-delivery contract with a 60-month period of performance for research and development, engineering and test work supporting the agency's technical offices. It says the agency "relies on" the laboratory to maintain essential capabilities "uniquely suited" to those offices and cites 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(3). A separate award notice for solicitation HR001127DE001, dated October 14, lists the same $499,800,000 for the laboratory.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs gives Duluth Travel a $29.1 million sole-source order to book air travel for veterans' medical trips
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The order covers commercial air booking for veterans who need medical transportation. The agency says it faced unacceptable delays and that Duluth already does general and beneficiary travel booking department-wide as a subcontractor under the current travel contract. It adds that Duluth is the only service-disabled veteran-owned small business on the underlying schedule. The award form lists a September 21 award date, 28 days before the justification was posted. The document says many veterans "cannot afford to purchase airline tickets up front."

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency expands CACI's financial-system task order without competition, saying no one else knows the system
meta: skipped the competition among existing contract holders
blocks.text: The action raises the ceiling and widens the scope of task order SP4709-26-F-0033 to move Defense Agencies Initiative reporting into the War Data Platform and to modernize its Oracle general ledger. The justification says CACI, as incumbent lead systems integrator, has "unmatched, highly specialized institutional and architectural knowledge," including roughly 4,500 global reports and 166 custom report views. It says any other source would need "an extensive discovery period."

blocks.title: Coast Guard buys more AT&T satellite service and removal work without competition because only AT&T can plug into its network
meta: only one company can do it
Department of Homeland Security (U.S. Coast Guard)
blocks.text: The modification to the Coast Guard's low-earth-orbit OneWeb contract adds bandwidth support and deinstallation services. The justification says "AT&T is the only source that can fulfill this requirement because the hardware and airtime services must be compatible with the existing CGONE Multiprotocol label switching (MPLS)." It notes AT&T won the Coast Guard's CGONE infrastructure contract competitively through the Enterprise Infrastructure Services vehicle.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Veterans Affairs keeps its Community Care Network contractor running in three regions for up to another year without competition
paragraphs: There are 13 new extension or bridge justifications: three Community Care Network regions (Region 2 was posted twice), one Army bridge, a Department of Health and Human Services-related continuity notice for Anthropic, and the shorter items listed below.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs extends Optum's Community Care Network contracts in Regions 1, 2 and 3 for up to a year without competition
meta: Optum Public Sector Solutions, Inc. (named on the award notices; redacted in the justifications)
urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: Each contract was awarded December 28, 2018, and its final option period expired September 30, 2026. The justifications cover October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027 for Region 1 (15 states and the District of Columbia), Region 2 (13 states) and Region 3 (11 states and territories). The agency says the replacement competition has been pushed back by two protests, more than 1,600 industry questions and "potential future litigation risks," and that only the current contractor can meet the need. The award forms list September 30 and give Optum amounts of $20,245,996,763.94 (Region 1), $22,490,596,798.99 (Region 2) and $28,798,457,761.61 (Region 3), but they do not make clear whether those are total contract values or this action's value. The notices were posted October 19.

blocks.title: Army gives Dawson Solutions a second six-month bridge at Fort Benning after finding its own work statement was flawed
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Army (Mission and Installation Contracting Command, Fort Moore)
blocks.text: The bridge to contract W911SF-21-C-0005 runs October 13, 2026 to April 12, 2027 for business operations and data services for the installation's Directorate of Public Works. A first six-month extension ran from October 13, 2025 to October 12, 2026. The justification says the competitive follow-on drew 43 proposals on September 30, then the requiring activity found the baseline work statement "materially flawed," which "creat[es] an unavoidable schedule gap." The agency says only the incumbent can keep services going in that window.

paragraphs: There were 545 new award notices, none left out as already reported. The three below are the standout awards, and the other 514 are routine, mostly Defense Logistics Agency parts buys.

The solicitation was listed earlier; this is the award.

sections.headline: Defense's $21.6 billion JWCC cloud solicitation limits the use of Defense data to train commercial AI models
paragraphs: There were 205 new solicitations and 1 earlier-reported solicitation left out; most flagged ones were repeats with only deadline or Q&A changes and are omitted. The first two cards come from documents read today on notices posted earlier.

blocks.title: Defense Information Systems Agency's JWCC UCM Core cloud solicitation sets a $21.6 billion ceiling and a 0.5% fee on other agencies' orders
meta: Solicitation (document read today on an earlier notice)
blocks.text: The solicitation says the "overall maximum cumulative dollar value of all task orders and authorizations" cannot exceed $21.6 billion, with a $100,000 minimum, and that outside agencies' contracting officers must add a 0.5% fee to each task order. The work statement describes a 10-year period, five years plus a five-year option, running "from December 2027 through December 2037." It requires clearances up to TS/SCI and at least three U.S. data centers within 18 months of award. It bars the contractor from using Defense data to "train, retrain, or augment its generally available commercial AI models" without written authorization.

blocks.title: Navy's 90-day tanker charter requires onboard security teams to defend ships against pirates and boarding forces
meta: Solicitation (document read today on a related earlier notice)
blocks.text: The charter terms cover "transportation and/or prepositioning of petroleum cargo (including, but not limited to hazardous cargoes, and general cargoes) and military readiness." The security clause requires the contractor to prevent boarding by a force of as many as 15 personnel and to defend against pirates or terrorists in 2 to 20 small vessels. Vessels must be under 20 years old, and the terms bar a vessel from going to Gibraltar on its next port call after leaving Spain. The document sits on solicitation N3220527R6008; a new tanker charter notice, N3220527R6013, was posted today.

meta: Department of the Navy (Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division)
blocks.text: The agreement would cover original-equipment hardware technical refresh packages and ship sets for the Navy's electronic chart system, Integrated Bridge System, ship control systems and machinery control systems. It covers cruisers, carriers, destroyers, frigates, command ships, littoral combat ships, amphibious ships and patrol craft. It follows agreement N6449821G4003 with Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation.

sections.headline: NASA says it is changing its approach to merging its deep space and near space networks under one contract
paragraphs: There were 47 new presolicitations and 1 repeat left out. Three cards are below, and about 37 are routine.

blocks.title: NASA revises its plan to run its Deep Space Network and Near Space Network under one contract
blocks.text: The notice says National Aeronautics and Space Administration assessed its Unified Network and Navigation Operations strategy and "determined that a more integrated approach better supports clear accountability." An industry day deck says the network is to be managed "as one network rather than two." It also says fixed-price, performance-based contracting is preferred and that the current contracts are cost-type.

meta: Department of the Navy (Naval Air Systems Command)
blocks.text: The firm-fixed-price contract would cover full-rate production, a Lot 1 base plus options for Lots 2 through 4 at 25 targets per lot. The notice projects award in the third quarter of fiscal 2030, with deliveries through fiscal 2036, sole-source to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation of San Diego.

footer.coverage_window: October 19, 2026 (Pacific), PM edition, covering SAM.gov notices posted October 18-19. USAspending is run only in the AM edition and is carried over by script.
footer.sources: OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov; USAspending.gov API; SAM.gov contract opportunities and their attached documents.
footer.known_gaps: No source errors reported. OMB Apportionments: no apportionment files approved October 14-19 and no new or changed spend plans identified. Document coverage: 1,910 attachments on 365 SAM.gov notices; 1,410 are queued for a later edition, 76 are access-restricted on SAM.gov and 1 has no extractable text (video/CAD); 2,355 files in all are queued for later editions, and about 990 links to outside portals (mostly DLA's DIBBS) were not followed.
